rubric.why: Identifies measurement as comparison against a standard.
rubric.description: Defines measurement as comparison of an unknown quantity with a standard quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning comparison of an unknown quantity with a standard quantity. Minor wording differences are acceptable; the idea of a widely accepted standard must be clear.

rubric.why: Names both parts of a measurement.
rubric.description: States that a measurement consists of a number and a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark only if both parts are named.

modelAnswer: A measurement is a process of comparison of an unknown quantity with a widely accepted standard quantity. A measurement consists of two parts, a number and a unit.

rubric.why: Explains that measurements can vary between people because their body-based measuring units differ.
rubric.description: States that measurements by different people may differ because of differences in hand, arm or step sizes, causing confusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the idea that people can obtain different measurements because their hands, arms or steps are different in size.

rubric.why: States the purpose of a standard: consistent results between people.
rubric.description: States that a standard is needed so that measurement by any person gives the same result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a standard avoids confusion by making measurements consistent.

modelAnswer: This measurement may result in confusion as the measurement of different people may differ from each other because of different sizes of their hands, arms or steps. To avoid such confusion, there is a need of a standard so that measurement by any person may result the same.

rubric.why: Gives the three base quantities named in the textbook answer.
rubric.description: Names length, mass and time as base quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all three base quantities.

rubric.why: Gives the three derived quantities named in the textbook answer.
rubric.description: Names speed, area and volume as derived quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all three derived quantities.

modelAnswer: Base quantities include length, mass and time. Derived quantities include speed, area and volume.

rubric.why: Checks the first five SI base quantities and their units and symbols.
rubric.description: Gives length—metre (m), mass—kilogram (kg), time—second (s), temperature—kelvin (K), and electric current—ampere (A).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming and giving the unit and symbol for these five base quantities.

rubric.why: Checks the remaining two SI base quantities and their units and symbols.
rubric.description: Gives intensity of light—candela (cd) and amount of substance—mole (mol).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming and giving the unit and symbol for both remaining base quantities.

modelAnswer: Length — metre (m); mass — kilogram (kg); time — second (s); temperature — kelvin (K); electric current — ampere (A); intensity of light — candela (cd); amount of substance — mole (mol).

rubric.why: Explains that prefixes simplify writing large and small quantities.
rubric.description: States that prefixes make large and small quantities simple to write down.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that prefixes simplify the writing of large and small quantities.

rubric.why: Checks the requested three sub-multiple and three multiple prefixes.
rubric.description: Names milli, centi and micro as sub-multiple prefixes, and kilo, mega and giga as multiple prefixes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming all three sub-multiple prefixes and all three multiple prefixes.

modelAnswer: The use of prefixes makes large and small quantities simple to write down. Three sub-multiple prefixes are milli (m), centi (c) and micro (μ). Three multiple prefixes are kilo (k), mega (M) and giga (G).

rubric.why: States that non-physical quantities cannot be measured with tools or instruments.
rubric.description: Explains that quantities such as love, fear or beauty cannot be measured using tools and instruments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that these quantities cannot be measured with instruments or tools.

rubric.why: Describes accepted qualitative ways to assess or compare such quantities.
rubric.description: States that they can be described qualitatively or compared using predetermined criteria, indices or survey techniques.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a qualitative method, comparison by criteria or indices, or survey techniques.

modelAnswer: Other quantities quoted above such as love, affection, fear, wisdom, and beauty cannot be measured using tools and instruments. They often pertain to the perception or interpretation of the observer. They can be described or qualitatively or compared using some pre-determined criteria, indices or through survey techniques.
